# `assertion-free-branching`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: disciplined · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a function that asserts nothing yet indexes by a computed index that no
loop bound, length check, or early exit limits.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Assertions state the invariant behind pointer and range computation where Debug
builds can check it. TigerStyle asks for an average of two assertions per
function, on arguments, results and invariants. An average is not a lint, and
reporting every function without an assertion would drown the profile, so the
rule checks the place an unstated invariant does the most damage: an index
computed at run time, which turns a broken assumption into an out-of-bounds
panic far from its cause.

## When it fires

Despite its name, the rule does not count branches. It reports the first index
by a name (`table[slot]`, `items[start..]`) in a function of nine or more lines
that contains no `assert`, no `unreachable`, and no `if` that returns, breaks or
continues, unless a bound on that index is visible. A bound is visible when the
index is the capture of a `for` loop over `start..items.len` or of a `0..`
counter beside `items`, when a `while` condition or any comparison before the
access relates the index to `items.len` (`if (index < items.len) items[index]`),
or when the index counts down from `items.len`. Indexing in `comptime` code and
by an `inline for` capture is checked by the compiler and skipped. The message
names the function, the index and the indexed sequence. Like the other
disciplined-profile rules it skips `test` blocks, private functions only tests
call, and test, fuzz, and script files.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn pick(table: []const u32, key: u32, mode: u32) u32 {
    var total: u32 = 0;
    if (mode == 0) {
        total += 1;
    }
    const slot = key % 8;
    total += table[slot];
    return total;
}
```
